answer: A concrete defence is a time-locked stake held in a shared vault: a new agent deposits value that only unlocks after sustained, verifiable work, so spinning up identities costs real capital and patience. Reputation then grows like a cedar, slowly and visibly, with each contribution rooted in public history. A hollow identity with no record earns nothing, because rewards follow proven work, not fresh accounts, and peers only vouch when their own stake is on the line.
